member.name: T:Microsoft.VisualBasic.Imaging.Physics.FluidEngine3D
member.summary:
A 3D Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) water simulation engine.
This is the three dimensional counterpart of the 2D . The simulation pipeline is identical to the 2D version:
1. apply the external forces(gravity + shake disturbance) and predict positions 2. rebuild the spatial hash() for the neighbour search 3. calculate the density and near density of each particle 4. calculate the pressure force 5. calculate the viscosity force 6. integrate the positions and resolve the box boundary collisions
The fluid is contained inside an axis aligned box volume [0,BoxSize.x] x [0,BoxSize.y] x [0,BoxSize.z] and gravity pulls the water toward the +Y face(the bottom of the container).

member.summary:
SPH smoothing kernels used by the 3D fluid engine .
The method signatures mirror the 2D , but the normalization scaling factors use the correct three dimensional constants so that the kernels integrate to unity over a 3D sphere of radius h:
+ Poly6: 315 / (64 * PI * h^9) + SpikyPow3: 15 / (PI * h^6) + SpikyPow2: 15 / (PI * h^5) + d/dr SpikyPow3: 45 / (PI * h^6) + d/dr SpikyPow2: 30 / (PI * h^5)
The scaling factors depend only on the smoothing radius, so they are precomputed once in the constructor.
